title: Combining Weather Forecast Aggregation and State-Space Models for Adaptive Probabilistic Electricity Load Forecasting (arXiv abstract page)
note: arXiv record, stat.AP, v1 of 15 Sep 2026 via the HAL proxy; de Vilmarest, Dumas (RTE R&D), Thorey. Abstract: adaptive GAM in state-space form (Viking) with a GAMLSS variance layer and a short-term correction; aggregating several weather providers improves point and probabilistic forecasts of French national load, most in extreme quantiles. No code or data link.

title: Combining Weather Forecast Aggregation and State-Space Models (full text): setup
note: Setup: French national load from RTE, hourly steps. Inputs: calendar, a tariff signal, forecast temperature and cloud cover from Meteo-France Arpege, ECMWF HRES and ECMWF EPS. Built for a 24-hour horizon (day d hour h given realised load of day d-1 hour h), then a per-horizon quantile correction from the last residual; plots run to about 70 hours.

title: Combining Weather Forecast Aggregation and State-Space Models (full text): point results
note: Table I, RMSE MW at 24 h, 2023 / 2024: Arpege 1117 / 1004; HRES 1112 / 1000; EPS 1251 / 1072; uniform 1097 / 957; time-invariant weights 1085 / 961; sequential aggregation 1090 / 958; additive stacking 1082 / 960. Authors: the rules are close, a uniform average gets most of the gain; they keep time-invariant weights fitted per horizon on 2021-2022.

title: Combining Weather Forecast Aggregation and State-Space Models (full text): probabilistic results
note: At 24 h, quantile-loss gain over single-provider Viking on Meteo-France input: aggregated Viking 13% at the 1% quantile, 9% at the 99%; Gaulss aggregation 1: 18% and 11%; Gaulss aggregation 2 (adds the spread of providers' point forecasts as a variance covariate): 21% and 17%. CRPS differences described as small; all methods described as calibrated.

title: Combining Weather Forecast Aggregation and State-Space Models (full text): single-provider numbers
note: Single provider, test period: CRPS 285 MW for GAM-Viking, 281 MW with the Gaulss layer (1.2% gain); 14% and 11% gain at the 1% and 99% quantiles. Standard deviation of differences between providers' temperature forecasts: 0.57 C (Arpege-HRES), 0.74 C (Arpege-EPS), 0.58 C (HRES-EPS).

title: Combining Weather Forecast Aggregation and State-Space Models (full text): what is absent
note: Not in the text: code or data availability, a repository, pre-registration, a significance test or interval, a naive or non-GAM baseline (every comparator is the same GAM-Viking on one provider). Train and test dates appear only in a figure; tables report 2023 and 2024. Fetched figure tables are plot reconstructions, not used for numbers.
